assertions.contract_summary: The workflow's only trigger is `pull_request` restricted to the `main` branch.
assertions.rationale: The durable contract (trigger is pull_request, branches restricted to main) is structural, but the raw regex locks four consecutive lines together with their exact block-style indentation and a block-sequence item (`      - main`). Empirically verified on the live workflow with temporary meaning-preserving mutations: rewriting the sequence in the equally valid and widely used flow style `branches: [main]` breaks it, restyling the block to 4-space nesting breaks it, and spelling out the default `types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]` breaks it -- none of which change what the workflow does. Unlike the single-line `^\s+key: value$` checks in this class, this one pins a multi-line serialization rather than a value, the raw form is brittle to presentation-only edits, so it should become a parsed-YAML structural check (`data['on']['pull_request']['branches'] == ['main']`); not converted in this PR.

The literal contains no whitespace, indentation or prose, so no reformatting of the workflow can break it. Category B.

assertions.contract_summary: The workflow declares neither a `schedule:` nor a `workflow_dispatch:` trigger.
assertions.rationale: A structural per-line-prefix negative regex with leading `^\s*`, so it is indentation-agnostic and matches on YAML key structure rather than on any prose. It keeps PR CI free of the production workflow's scheduled and manually dispatched triggers. Matches this suite's established `structural regex, not a raw substring` B precedent.

Empirically verified with temporary meaning-preserving mutations of the live workflow: inserting an explanatory comment line between the key and its child (`permissions:` / `  # read-only: CI never writes to the repository` / `  contents: read`) breaks it, and restyling the block to 4-space nesting breaks it, while neither changes the granted permissions. The same tranche's single-line field checks survive both. The value is structural but its two-line raw form is brittle, so it should become a parsed-YAML check on the top-level permissions mapping; not converted in this PR.

assertions.contract_summary: The workflow never grants `contents: write` anywhere.
assertions.rationale: A negative check on a structural permission field/value token drawn from Actions' closed read/write/none vocabulary. It is the load-bearing half of the read-only contract: it also covers job-level permission blocks that a top-level-only check would miss. Empirically verified: flipping the live workflow to `contents: write` fails this method. Category B (`permission field/value`).

assertions.contract_summary: The checkout step pins `actions/checkout` to the full commit SHA `3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1`, documented as v7.0.1.
assertions.rationale: This single raw line welds two things of different kinds: the structural supply-chain contract (action identifier plus full 40-hex commit SHA, which is load-bearing) and the trailing `# v7.0.1` YAML comment, which GitHub Actions ignores entirely and which is editorial text a maintainer may reword. Empirically verified with temporary meaning-preserving mutations: rewording the comment to `# pinned to v7.0.1`, dropping the comment, or widening the space before `#` each breaks this assertion although the workflow runs identically (appending after the comment does not, since it is a substring check -- confirming the brittleness is in the comment's exact rendering). Per the established rule this is not `B just because it contains a structural element`: it should be split into a structural check on `uses: actions/checkout@<sha>` plus a separate version-comment check; not converted in this PR. It is not D -- a currently pinned action SHA is the current workflow structural contract, not historical acceptance evidence.

assertions.contract_summary: The Python setup step requests the `python-version` input as the string `3.12`.
assertions.rationale: PR #93 round 1 (Blocker 1): B -> C. The durable contract is that the `python-version` action input is the string `3.12`, and requiring SOME quoting is structural -- unquoted `3.12` is a YAML float, the bug class that silently turns `3.10` into `3.1`. But the raw regex goes further and pins the double-quoted presentation: the equally valid `python-version: '3.12'` denotes the identical string yet fails it, so the check is brittle to a quote-style change that leaves workflow semantics untouched. Fixing DOUBLE quotes specifically is presentation, not contract. Should become a parsed-YAML or quote-normalized structural check on the input's string value; not converted in this PR.
